newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money edges down to 10.5/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money edges down to 10.5/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged down to 10.5/11.0 percent from 12.5/13.5 percent on the back of ample liquidity in the money market, dealers said on Tutesday.
One local bank dealer said ample liquidity might have resulted from a return of civil servants' salaries to Jakarta after they were transferred to other cities last week.
He said the money was usually pooled in Jakarta.
"This might explain brisk supply despite relatively neutral central bank money policy this morning," the dealer said.
Dealers said swap rates and longer-term money were little changed despite the approaching month-end.
They said operators remained calm and this was reflected in stable rates for all periods of interbank money and swap rates.
The average overnight interbank money on Monday was 11.22 percent, compared with 11.20 percent on Friday.
